title: Velarivirus Coverage Audit
eyebrow: LowVan · Velarivirus module · 29 September 2026 · rescue backfilled 1 October 2026 · ORF1a, RdRp and accessories 2 October 2026
h1: Does the grapevine leafroll-associated virus 7 module actually work?
standfirst: Velarivirus is the smallest of the three closterovirid modules — grapevine leafroll-associated virus 7, cordyline virus 1–4, Actinidia virus 1 and a handful more. It is also the only one carrying a thaumatin-like protein, which no other closterovirid genus has.

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: Seven features on one long RNA: a replicase polyprotein and RdRp, then the quintuple gene block — HSP70 homolog, HSP90 homolog, CPm, CP — plus a thaumatin-like protein.

blocks.html: Self-recall is a floor, not a validation: a profile that cannot recover its own training data will certainly not recover anything new, but recovering it proves very little. The held-out numbers are in §05 and §06.

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: Binned from the BV-BRC protein dump, with the accessory names treated as untrustworthy.

blocks.html: The accessories are named by mass, and a mass is not a homology group. Where two masses turned out to be one protein they were merged; where one mass covered two non-homologous groups they were numbered apart.
400 for the replicase polyprotein, 300 for the RdRp, 150 for the HSP70 and HSP90 homologs, 80 for the coat proteins, 25–60 for the accessories by length.

sections.title: Does it call the proteins?
sections.lede: Measured against real genomes for the first time.

blocks.html: HSP90 was shipping without copy_num on the assumption that only part of the genus carries it. This backfill is the first time the module has been measured against real genomes, and it calls on 91.3% — over the 0.85 threshold. Corrected. CPM at 58.7% and the thaumatin-like protein at 35.3% correctly keep none.

35 of the 46 flags are “too many HSPs”, 18 are a missing essential feature. “Genome has too many HSPs” is the dominant flag, and it is a different thing from a duplicate call: it means one feature's profile matched at several places in a genome, not that two features collided. The duplicate-call audit is clean for this module.

An earlier report in this session called this module defective. It was wrong. A duplicate-call check without a containment floor reported RDRP as 79% nested inside POLY and the thaumatin-like protein as 66% inside HSP90. Adjacent genes in a compact viral genome overlap routinely; with an 80% containment floor applied, Velarivirus has no exact duplicates and no nested calls at all.
No mature peptides. The replicase is a polyprotein whose cleavage sites are not documented for this genus in a form that can be located from the sequence.

The evaluation is a sample. Measured on a random sample of up to 150 genomes at ≥6 kb (seed 29). Annotation costs about 86 seconds per genome, and 150 is ample for the decision it feeds: the test for copy_num is whether a feature is called on at least 85% of routed genomes, estimated to within about ±6 points at that sample size.

The homology rescue has now run on this module. Completed 1 October 2026, closing the item deferred on 30 September. rescue_unassigned.py takes every protein no annotation-string rule matched, blastp’s it against this module’s own collections and adopts each into the feature it matches at ≥80% identity over ≥60% of the query, refusing everything below that rather than sweeping it into a grab-bag. It had never run on this module because it crashed on the trailing tab BV-BRC writes into uniq.seq. 110 of 683 unassigned sequences were adopted; the training set went 627 → 705 sequences (+12%) and the profile set 67 → 69. The only module where the rescue is a net loss, and the smallest adoption rate of the six at 16%. One genome regressed: HSP90 is called at 497–505 aa against a collection minimum of 506 and a source annotation of 513 (p60 protein, genome 1654603). The cause is not shorter training data — all 22 adopted sequences are inside the window — but a change in HSP90’s clustering, 8 alignments to 7, whose merged consensus places the N-terminus further in. The real gap here is declared features, not training data: of 573 sequences the rescue refused, 185 are hypothetical protein and 85 are named by mass — p25, p21, p60, p27, p4, P22 across Velarivirus and Olivavirus. The module declares seven features and not one accessory, so those proteins have nowhere to go and no rescue can place them. Measured against a control — the shipped module scored on the same 64 genomes with the current JSON — the rescue moved genuinely-clean from 50.0% to 48.4% (0 genome(s) improved, 1 regressed). The earlier comparison against measurements/quality.tsv was discarded: that table predates the 30 September copy_num and vocabulary edits, which on some modules dominate the rescue entirely.

ORF1a and the RdRp were rebuilt from the genome, 2 October 2026. POLY held three different things at once — ORF1a, the ORF1a+ORF1b frameshift fusion, and partials of both — and no threshold separates them: every member has some C-terminal RdRp-like hit and only the long ones have a real one. So ORF1A is extracted by coordinate instead, tblastn locating the reading frame and the walk going to the ATG and to the in-frame stop. On Ampelovirus genome 126071.15 that is ATG 490 → TAG 6448–6450, 1986 aa, matching the tblastn exactly. The frameshift is +1, measured not assumed — frames 1→2, which by the kit's own rule reads as +1, with the subject jumping 6447→6449 so base 6448 is skipped. The partitioning note saying −1 was wrong. ORF1b is not a separate product here, unlike the coronaviruses where it carries NSP12–16: the 524 aa portion matches an RDRP collection member end to end at 99.6%. And there is no ATG for it — the only one nearby is in ORF1a's frame — so the RdRp's N-terminus is made by the frameshift, which by the kit's N-terminus rule makes it a mat_peptide carried by special: transcript_edit with 52 junction-spanning nucleotide references and no PSSM at all.

24 accessory features were added, 2 October 2026. The unassigned pool had never been clustered for this module — UNASSIGNED_TRACKING.tsv recorded it and nothing downstream read the file. Running the kit's own accessory_clusters over it (mmseqs at 25% identity) produced homology groups that a string rule cannot reach: on Velarivirus, 21 sequences all exactly 157 aa with half of them labelled hypothetical protein. Groups that produced no profile are deliberately not declared, and groups measured to be homologous to each other were merged — a first pass ran at a member floor of 5 against the kit's default of 12 and over-split seven features across three modules.

Measured on the same 64 genomes scored after the homology rescue: genuinely clean 48.4% → 48.4%, features called 362 → 667 (0 genome(s) improved, 0 regressed). The new accessories carry no copy_num, so they name proteins without counting against the verdict — which is why the clean rate can hold while the feature count rises sharply. What this does not show is whether the new calls are right. It shows they fire, do not collide and trip no quality check; whether a group is one protein correctly identified is a curation question.

The copy_num correction is the finding. It was invisible until the module was run against genomes, which is the whole argument for measuring essentiality rather than assigning it: a feature believed to be genus-partial turned out to be present on nine genomes in ten.
Seven of seven features have profiles and call at 95.8–100% of their own collections; five are essential on measurement, and the sixth was corrected here.
The largest collapse ratio in the whole report series. The module's vocabulary is complete after four genomes; the source reaches 161 distinct strings and is still climbing at 150.
